newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, US clarify obstacles to veterinary pact.
newsitem.headline: EU, US clarify obstacles to veterinary pact.

text.p: Senior European Commission and U.S. officials discussed on Tuesday obstacles to an agreement on mutual recognition of veterinary standards.

Washington is concerned that an estimated $2.0 billion trade in veterinary and phytosanitary products could be disrupted when the EU harmonises import rules in the 15 member states on January 1, 1997.
"Views were clarified. There was a good atmosphere but there are a number of problems to be solved," Corrado Pirzio-Biroli, head of the Commission team told Reuters after 4 1/2 hours of talks.
Pirzio-Biroli, chief aide to EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler, said that European Commission and U.S. officials will hold technical talks on Wednesday to identify outstanding difficulties.

"We shall try to find bridges," he said, adding that EU member states would not agree on transitional arrangements after January 1, 1997, unless sufficient progress had been made by the end of the year.
The U.S team was led by Paul Drazek, trade adviser to U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman.
